note: A guide for packing, not a required list: take what suits you. Your marks are stored only on this phone.

i: Passport for travel abroad — valid for more than 6 months. A photo of the first page — on your phone.
Saudi Arabia visa (e-visa) — a printout, and a PDF on your phone.
Nusuk — signing in to your account works; Umrah and Rawdah permits saved as screenshots.
Kazakhstan national ID card — for the trip back and for the bank.
Cash in riyals for food, taxis, shopping; some dollars or euros for the transfer. Exchanging money in the city is better than at the airport.
Visa or Mastercard bank card. Tell your bank that you are travelling.
Copies of your passport and visa — kept apart from the originals.
Ihram — two sheets (if the organiser does not provide them). A belt bag for ihram — optional.
Ihram sandals — open at the top of the foot and at the heel. Worn in, not new.
Comfortable walking shoes — you walk many kilometres a day.
Long shirts or qamis, trousers — for the number of days; the hotel usually has laundry.
A warm sweater — it is cold on the plane and in the mosques because of the air conditioning.
Underwear and socks for every day.
A sun hat and sunglasses — outside of ihram.
A small backpack and a shoe bag for the mosque.
Razor or trimmer, scissors — for after Umrah. Checked luggage only.
Unscented wet wipes and hand sanitiser.
Vaseline or unscented cream — against chafing in ihram.

groups.t: First aid kit · a guide, not medical advice
i: Your regular medicines with a supply for a few extra days, in the original packaging; for prescription medicines — a prescription or a doctor's note. If you have a chronic illness, are pregnant or have allergies, agree the list with your doctor.
Fever and pain relief (paracetamol or ibuprofen).
Lozenges or throat spray — the air in the Haram is dry and air-conditioned.
For an upset stomach — rehydration salts (electrolytes), an adsorbent.
Travel sickness medicine — if you get sick on buses.
Power bank — carry-on only, not in checked luggage.
Adapter for type G sockets (three flat pins) — for Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Apps — install them at home over Wi-Fi: Nusuk, this guide (open it once with internet and add it to your home screen), offline maps, a translator, your bank's app.
Connection — a local SIM card with your passport, or an eSIM in advance. Turn off mobile data until you buy one.
Snacks for the road — nuts, dates, bars.
Prayer beads (tasbih). The Quran is easier to carry on your phone.
A notebook — who to make du'a for. The guide has its own list in the “Du'a” section.
A suitcase lock and a tag with your name and phone number.
A foldable bag — for gifts on the way back.
Valuables, jewellery, large amounts of cash (large sums must be declared).
Many printed religious books — customs checks them.
Medicines with strong substances without documents — check with your doctor and the rules of the country you are entering.
E-cigarettes — check whether the country you are entering bans them.
Passport, visa, tickets — at hand; screenshots of the QR codes from Nusuk taken.
Suitcase and hand luggage weighed according to your ticket's allowance.
Phone charged, guide added to the home screen.
Nails and hair done — fewer worries before ihram.
At home: keys, money for the family. Ask your loved ones for forgiveness; pay off your debts or come to an agreement about them.
